author.heading: About Daniel Dennett
author.bio: Daniel Dennett (1942–2024) was an American philosopher whose work connected philosophy of mind with cognitive science and evolutionary biology. He taught at Tufts for more than fifty years and directed its Center for Cognitive Studies; his books include Consciousness Explained and Breaking the Spell.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Sweet Dreams revisits Dennett’s account of consciousness in light of later scientific and philosophical work. Its publisher describes a model in which consciousness emerges from distributed processes rather than a single central theater. The cells sentence illustrates the explanatory contrast between a whole person and the parts from which a person is composed.
